body:
## Change

Building gradients currently expand across every reachable cell even when callers only need nearby positions. This adds opt-in propagation that stops after the requested cost layer and resumes its retained queue on later queries. Initialization and seed scanning stay eager; round-trip field construction still finishes the parent building field.

- One expansion kernel serves both eager and lazy searches. Point queries finish whole cost layers to preserve equal-distance movement choices. The public array accessor always completes the field; private scalar/movement adapters resolve automatically.
- Frozen terrain inputs and the existing refresh/idle-eviction policy preserve cached routing answers. Saving finishes pending fields and writes the existing complete-field representation; no save/replay/network version changes.
- Includes API and telemetry documentation, oracle/frozen-terrain regressions, and Linux/Windows CI coverage for lazy save continuation. Measurement-only instrumentation is excluded.

Defaults off. Enable with `--run-game --lazy-building-gradients true`, or `GLOB2_LAZY_BUILDING_GRADIENTS=1` for legacy entry points. No gameplay or pacing changes are intended.

## Validation and evidence

[Retained fixtures, checksums, saves, commands, logs and benchmark data](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/ecc77866349e3f48ebad5712dff44eeeb08546d3) are on a separate evidence branch, outside this PR's diff.

Native macOS release client/server builds and the gradient-oracle, invalidation, immobile-unit and save-safety harnesses pass. Four games (65,442 ticks per mode) match the original baseline's per-tick checksum sidecars and initial/final saves exactly in both modes. Another 1,024-tick old-save continuation matches simulation checksums; one run has a saved diagnostic-value mismatch from the pre-existing Maxima `policy_bids[6]` out-of-bounds telemetry read. The evidence retains that mismatch and a matching repeat; it is not hidden by normalization.

## Performance and limits

The controlled **162-run study of d50968d06** compared the original baseline with that lazy implementation in disabled and enabled modes. Each scenario has 6 or 12 matched repetitions, with all six mode orders balanced. Timings ran serially on an Apple M3 on AC power; no outcome-based exclusions. Positive values below mean less total headless process CPU.

| Workload | Net CPU saved vs original baseline | Approx. 95% timing interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Arena 128², 2 players | 4.3% | 4.0–4.6% |
| Arena 256², 2 players | 2.5% | 2.3–2.6% |
| Arena 512², 4 players | 8.3% | 7.5–9.0% |
| Lakes 256², 4 players | 8.1% | 7.9–8.3% |
| Arena 256², additional seed, 4 players | 2.2% | 2.1–2.4% |
| Lakes 256², additional seed, 4 players | 3.6% | 3.1–4.0% |
| Lakes 256², four checkpoints | 7.7% | 7.5–8.0% |

The earlier two-run 256² slowdown did not recur; its raw measurements remain retained. The larger study supersedes those estimates without attributing a definite cause to the earlier variability. Intervals quantify repeatability for these fixed games, not the range across all games or platforms.

Building-gradient scopes fall by 30–39%. With lazy mode disabled, the PR costs about 0.5–1.0% CPU in three scenarios and is close to baseline in the others. Enabling lazy mode adds about 0.4–6.5 MiB peak RSS relative to the same binary with it disabled.

Four synchronous checkpoints increase mean serialization from 92.8 to 105.4 ms: **+12.6 ms/save** (95% interval +3.4 to +21.8 ms), while the entire checkpoint run still saves 7.7% CPU. GUI asynchronous autosave/frame latency remains unmeasured.

[The complete timing report and evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/e6194e49895063a2d254e054a50d61dd2bed97cc/timing-study) contains the fixed plan, all 162 raw measurements, generated map fixtures, logs, analysis, plots and reproduction scripts. No game code changed for this expanded study.

## Safer query API and remaining costs

[API cleanup, renewed validation and profiling evidence](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/edf80b22276a345167bbc837b0d38fef9b11d1db/api-profile) covers 7d2dcaf1c. Full-field access always returns a completed array; point and movement queries resolve internally. Cache refresh/use timestamps, eviction, search work and save layout stay unchanged. The new boundary regression covers all seven swim classes. Native harnesses, all four per-tick checksum/save comparisons in both modes, and the old-save continuation pass again.

This follow-up compares **two lazy implementations**. Its 40 uninstrumented timing runs do not establish a small overall gain or loss from the API cleanup; initial power transitions and later timing variation are retained and reported. It does not negate the earlier eager-versus-lazy benefit. Gradient build and actual-extension call counts are identical before/after in every workload.

Twelve separate diagnostic runs put initialization at **33–44%** of remaining building-gradient time, seed/water scanning at **7–10%**, and queue setup around **0.02–0.10%**. Queue growth is a **0.46–5.19% subset** of the other phases; destruction was not isolated. This favors experimenting with fewer preparation passes before a custom allocator. Instrumentation is excluded from production code. The hardware trace uses broad bottleneck counters and does not provide direct L1/L2 miss rates.

Linux and Windows checks pass on the API cleanup commit; the browser build is still running. Full-game cross-platform equivalence for these lazy workloads and interactive play remain unverified; CI builds/harnesses alone do not establish those. The feature stays opt-in for review.
title: Add opt-in lazy building gradient propagation
